## Launch environment and rendezvous (`MASTER_PORT`, `BACKEND`) {#sec-ch14-launch}

sources: src/layout/layout.cpp, src/layout/layout.hpp, src/mesh/mesh.cpp, src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp, api/pd-run, tests/test_process_group.cpp

### Summary

The launch settings are not read from the YAML card. `LayoutOptionsImpl`'s constructor reads them from the
environment that `torchrun` (or `pd-run`) sets for each process. The `distribute` block of the card supplies the layout
and the block counts (@sec-ch03-layouts). A single process with no `MASTER_PORT` picks a random port and never
opens a store. A run that implies more than one process and has no `MASTER_PORT` stops in the constructor, because
the ranks could not find one another.

::: {.callout-note title="At a glance"}
**What**: one operating-system process per rank, started by `torchrun` or `api/pd-run`; the processes meet at a
c10d `TCPStore` on `MASTER_ADDR:MASTER_PORT`, and each holds `blocks_per_process` blocks. **Switch**: environment
`RANK`, `WORLD_SIZE`, `PROCESS_RANK`, `PROCESS_WORLD_SIZE`, `LOCAL_RANK`, `MASTER_ADDR`, `MASTER_PORT`, `DEVICE`,
`DEVICE_ID`, `BACKEND`. **Default**: one process, `MASTER_ADDR=127.0.0.1`, `DEVICE=cpu`, a random port in
$[29500, 29600]$. **Requires**: `MASTER_PORT` whenever more than one process is implied. **Order**: n/a.
**Defining equation**: @eq-ch14-launch-rank.
:::

### Derivation

None: this scheme is bookkeeping. The one relation it fixes is the global block rank. A process of rank $p$ holding
$b$ blocks gives its local block $\ell \in [0, b)$ the rank

$$
r = p\,b + \ell, \qquad p = \lfloor r/b \rfloor, \qquad \ell = r \bmod b ,
$$ {#eq-ch14-launch-rank}

and the global block count is the process count times $b$. @eq-ch14-launch-rank is `global_block_rank`,
`owner_process_rank` and `local_block_index` ({{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutOptionsImpl >}}).
A port of the three functions confirms the round trip $r \to (p, \ell) \to r$ for $b = 1, \dots, 16$ [check
`src/snapy_report/ch14/launch_check.py`, output `launch_check.out`, `[C1]`], that the $P\,b$ pairs fill
$0, \dots, P\,b - 1$ with no gap or repeat (`[C2]`), and that $b < 1$ acts as $b = 1$ (`[C3]`).

### Numerical method

The constructor resolves each setting in a fixed order
(`LayoutOptionsImpl`, {{< code src/layout/layout.cpp LayoutOptionsImpl::LayoutOptionsImpl >}}):

| setting | read from, in order | default |
|---|---|---|
| backend | `BACKEND` | `default_backend()`, @sec-ch14-backends |
| process rank | `PROCESS_RANK`, then `RANK` | 0 |
| process count | `PROCESS_WORLD_SIZE`, then `WORLD_SIZE` | 1 |
| block rank | `RANK`, then the process rank | the process rank |
| local rank | `LOCAL_RANK` | 0 |
| store address | `MASTER_ADDR` | `127.0.0.1` |
| store port | `MASTER_PORT` | random in $[29500, 29600]$ if one process; else an error |
| device | `DEVICE` | `cpu` |
| device index | `DEVICE_ID` | $-1$, meaning `LOCAL_RANK` |

: Launch settings and where `LayoutOptionsImpl` reads them. {#tbl-ch14-launch-env}

The block rank and the global size from the environment are provisional. `MeshImpl::reset` overwrites them for each
local block with @eq-ch14-launch-rank and sets the global size to the process count times `blocks_per_process`
({{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshImpl::reset >}}). `blocks_per_process` comes from
`distribute: blocks_per_process` in the card, default 1 (`MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml`, {{< code src/mesh/mesh.cpp MeshOptionsImpl::from_yaml >}}).
The store is opened only when the process count is above 1 (`use_process_group`,
{{< code src/layout/layout.hpp LayoutImpl::use_process_group >}}); @sec-ch14-backends describes it.

The device string of a block is `cuda:<DEVICE_ID>`, or `cuda:<LOCAL_RANK>` when `DEVICE_ID` is negative, if `DEVICE`
is `cuda`; otherwise it is the `DEVICE` value (`device_str`, {{< code src/mesh/meshblock_options.cpp MeshBlockOptionsImpl::device_str >}}).

`api/pd-run <n> <executable> [args]` is a single-node launcher. It starts $n$ processes and exports, for each, `RANK`
and `PROCESS_RANK` equal to the loop index, `WORLD_SIZE` and `PROCESS_WORLD_SIZE` equal to $n$, `LOCAL_RANK` equal to
the index modulo the number of entries of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` (default `0,1,2,3`), and `DEVICE_ID` equal to that
entry. Its own defaults are `BACKEND=ucx` and `DEVICE=cpu` (`launch_rank`, [`pd-run:113-138`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/api/pd-run#L113-L138)). With no `MASTER_PORT`, it
tries up to 32 random ports in $[20000, 40000)$ and takes the first that `ss` does not show as listening; without
`ss`, or after 32 busy ports, it takes $20000 + (\mathrm{pid} \bmod 20000)$ with the script's process id, unchecked
(`choose_master_port`, [`pd-run:39-51`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/api/pd-run#L39-L51)).

The cases are gtest cases of `LayoutOptions` and `ProcessGroupContext`
([`test_process_group.cpp:74-192`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/tests/test_process_group.cpp#L74-L192)):

1. `DefaultsToPlatformCommunicationBackend` and `UsesBackendEnvironmentVariable`;
2. `IgnoresYamlBackend` and `BackendEnvironmentOverridesYamlBackend`;
3. `RandomizesDefaultMasterPortWhenEnvUnset`;
4. two cases:
   - `RequiresMasterPortForMultiProcessWhenEnvUnset`,
   - `RequiresMasterPortWhenWorldSizeImpliesMultiProcess`;
5. `UsesProvidedMasterPortForMultiProcess`;
6. `ProcessGroupContext.SkipsSingleProcessCommunication`.

These are unit tests of the option parsing in one process. They do not start a multi-process rendezvous; the
two-rank tests of the following sections do, through `torchrun --no-python --nproc-per-node=2`
(`add_test`, [`macro_setup_parallel_test.cmake:28-32`](https://github.com/chengcli/snapy/blob/e894700ff7aee30b52882e5202b16461413780b0/cmake/macros/macro_setup_parallel_test.cmake#L28-L32)). Their pass
status at the pin was not run for this chapter.

### Limits

::: {.callout-warning title="Limits"}
- `pd-run` exports `BLOCKS_PER_PROCESS`, but nothing under `src/` reads it. Only `test_exchange` and two test
  runners read it; a run takes its block count from `distribute: blocks_per_process` in the card.
- `pd-run` sets `DEVICE_ID` to the entry of `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES` and also exports `CUDA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`
  unchanged. CUDA numbers the visible devices from 0, so with a list that does not start at 0 (for example `2,3`)
  `DEVICE_ID=2` names a device the process cannot see. This is read from the script and has not been run.
- `pd-run` starts every process on the local host; it has no multi-node mode.
:::

The `BLOCKS_PER_PROCESS` readers are `test_exchange.cpp`, `run_exchange_decomp.py` and `run_exchange_backend.py`
(`BLOCKS_PER_PROCESS`, {{< code tests/test_exchange.cpp main >}}).
